steps.what: Evaluate chronic pain, function and the patient's treatment experience
Manage chronic pain with an individual care approach and reassessment

tasks.design: Retain assessment and shared management of chronic pain. The clinical record system {OTHER} supplies context; a model does not assign a pain cause or choose treatment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Chronic pain involves function, experience and uncertainty beyond a single score.
tasks.enabler_now: Record access supports context without replacing the clinical encounter.
tasks.still_hard: Symptoms, goals and response can vary and require continuing reassessment.
tasks.human_edge: The physician listens without reducing the patient's experience to a score and seeks appropriate specialist support.
tasks.altitude: Chronic-pain management responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify functional goals in a pain-management handoff
reach.learn: Shared outcome descriptions and referral scope

evidence.claim: Keeping individual chronic-pain assessment and management human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is clinical evaluation and management, excluding separate medical-record writing and prescription entry.
No structured pain-cause label, automatic treatment or new machine input is assumed.
Existing clinical references remain; no custom decision system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
unknowns: Pain case mix and referral access
research_questions: Which changes in pain and function require reassessment of the management approach?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Clinical evaluation and management remain counted; note-writing savings are outside this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide medical coverage at games and competitions

steps.what: Attend games and evaluate activity-related injuries or medical conditions
Provide on-site treatment and arrange further care when required

tasks.design: Retain physical event coverage, immediate evaluation and treatment. Existing event protocols in {DOCS} support the physician; no remote model substitutes for on-site medical presence or response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Coverage requires being available where injuries occur.
tasks.enabler_now: Administrative technology does not remove the physical response requirement.
tasks.still_hard: Rapidly changing conditions and limited resources require immediate clinical judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The physician observes the athlete directly and acts within the actual event setting.
tasks.altitude: Event coverage responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Give a clear event-to-emergency care handoff
reach.learn: Local event escalation and handoff arrangements

evidence.claim: Retaining on-site event medical coverage is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is required event presence and care, not travel booking or record production. Required availability is not removable administrative waste.
No free structured triage category or automated clinical action is assumed.
Existing event protocols and medical equipment remain; no custom tool is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no process changes. The split describes distinct assessment and intervention activity without claiming reduced standby coverage.
unknowns: Coverage duties and event emergency arrangements
research_questions: What on-site response and availability duties must the coverage arrangement preserve?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Event presence, assessment and treatment remain counted; no idle-time or machine-runtime saving is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain nutrition, hydration, supplements and medication consequences

steps.what: Inform athletes about nutrition, hydration, supplements and possible medication consequences

tasks.design: Retain personal explanation of nutrition, hydration, supplements and medication consequences. Current references in {DOCS} support the discussion; a generated answer does not replace checking the athlete's understanding or specialist referral.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions depend on actual products, health circumstances and activity.
tasks.enabler_now: Reference availability does not establish a shorter counselling conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete supplement information and uncertain claims need careful qualification.
tasks.human_edge: The physician identifies limits of available information and avoids unsupported reassurance.
tasks.altitude: Information and counselling responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.task: Formulate a focused specialist nutrition referral

evidence.claim: Keeping personalised athlete health explanations human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is explanation and questions, not prescribing or writing a dietary programme. General injury-prevention counselling is separately described and repeated conversation time must be assigned once.
No free structured supplement composition or automated safety conclusion is assumed.
Existing references suffice; no custom advice tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
research_questions: Which unanswered product or medication questions require clarification or specialist input?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Personal explanation and understanding checks remain; no hypothetical leaflet production is counted.

tasks.short: Inform authorised parties about athlete medical conditions

steps.what: Verify what medical information may be shared and with whom
Inform authorised coaches or trainers within the verified disclosure scope

tasks.design: Retain disclosure checks and direct communication through {TELEPHONY}. The physician shares only the permitted information with the verified recipient; no automated medical-status feed to coaches or trainers is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Interest in an athlete's condition does not itself establish permission to receive medical details.
tasks.enabler_now: Message generation does not resolve disclosure authority or context.
tasks.still_hard: Athlete preferences, pressure from others and practical care needs can conflict.
tasks.human_edge: The physician protects confidentiality while explaining authorised restrictions clearly.
tasks.altitude: Disclosure responsibility and communication time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Clarify permitted practical restrictions without requesting unnecessary details

evidence.claim: Retaining recipient and disclosure checks with clinical communication is an E1 assessment from model knowledge, not a detailed statement of national disclosure law.

assumptions: Boundary is information disclosure to third parties, excluding advice given directly to the athlete.

The physician establishes recipient identity, permitted content, purpose and limits in s1; all 35 hours remain, with manual clarification if authority is unclear. No machine action or free consent flag is assumed.
Use existing communication facilities; no custom disclosure tool is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. Applicable national rules and organisational disclosure arrangements require customer confirmation.
research_questions: How does the physician verify the permitted scope before communicating practical restrictions?

already_counted.description: Disclosure-scope verification and final communication check

approvals.approved_version: Exact recipient, medical statements and practical restrictions within the checked disclosure scope; changes require a new physician check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Disclosure verification and communication retain all time; no automated release or message-copying saving is claimed.
